sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE UPR OH VLY TO E TX
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... NRN PLAINS UPR LOW WILL BE QSTNRY ON SATURDAY AS THE ATTENDANT TROUGH CONTINUES TO DEEPEN THROUGHOUT WRN NORTH AMERICA. MID-LVL SPEED MAX CURRENTLY MOVING INTO THE TX BIG BEND REGION ALONG SERN FLANKS OF THE TROUGH WILL TRANSLATE TO THE MID-MS VLY BY SATURDAY EVENING AS ADDITIONAL ENERGY DIGS INTO NRN MEXICO. AT THE SFC...PRIMARY BAROCLINIC ZONE WILL REMAIN FROM THE CNTRL GRTLKS SWWD TO CNTRL MO AND NCNTRL TX.

sections.title: LWR OH VLY TO E TX
sections.text: BACKBUILDING MCS OVER THE LWR OH VLY AND MID-SOUTH REGION AT 12Z SATURDAY WILL LIKELY WEAKEN AS CORE OF THE STRONGEST LLJ SHIFTS NEWD INTO THE UPR OH VLY. THIS WILL ALLOW THE AIR MASS TO RECOVER AS RICH LLVL MOISTURE/INSTABILITY ATTEMPTS TO SURGE WNW TO THE AFOREMENTIONED BAROCLINIC ZONE. SVR TSTMS WERE ALREADY DVLPG OVER SWRN TX IN RESPONSE TO THE MID-LEVEL IMPULSE MOVING OUT OF NRN MEXICO. THESE STORMS WILL LIKELY BE ONGOING OVER THE HILL COUNTRY/CNTRL TX AT 12Z AND MAY TEMPORARILY WEAKEN. HOWEVER...AS THE MID-LVL SPEED MAX CONTINUES ENE...LLVL SLY FLOW WILL RESPOND AND RESULT IN A RAPID ENHANCEMENT OF WAA FROM THE SABINE RVR VLY NWD INTO THE MID-SOUTH BY EVENING. THIS WILL RESULT IN BOTH A REINTENSIFICATION OF EXISTING TX ACTIVITY AND ADDITIONAL STORM INITIATION FROM THE ARKLATEX NEWD INTO THE LWR OH VLY THROUGH THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT HOURS. DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL BE MORE THAN ADEQUATE FOR SUPERCELLS ACROSS A BROAD REGION AND ALL FACETS OF SVR WEATHER WILL BE POSSIBLE. TORNADO RISK WILL BE HIGHEST IN THE MDT RISK REGION. HERE...THE LLVL SHEAR IS FCST TO BE COMPARATIVELY WEAKER THAN FRIDAY...BUT SUFFICIENT VEERING IN THE LOWEST FEW KM...FAVORABLE 0-3KM CAPE AND LOW LCLS WILL MAINTA

sections.title: UPR OH VLY
sections.text: LINEAR MCS WILL BE ONGOING AT 12Z SATURDAY ACROSS PORTIONS OF IND AND CNTRL KY THAT WILL CONTINUE ENE TOWARD THE UPR OH VLY BY AFTN. SOME INCREASE IN LLVL MOISTURE WILL OCCUR AHEAD OF THE STORMS OWING TO A 45-50 KT LLJ. SOME HEATING AND MODEST DESTABILIZATION MAY CONTRIBUTE TO AT LEAST A MARGINAL SVR THREAT /DMGG WIND OR ISOLD TORNADO/ THROUGH EARLY EVENING. THEREAFTER...CORE OF THE LLJ WILL WEAKEN AND REFOCUS FARTHER W RESULTING IN A CORRESPONDING DECREASE IN THE SVR THREAT AFTER DARK. ..RACY/COOK/HURLBUT.. 05/01/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: HIGH AMPLITUDE CNTRL STATES TROUGH WILL MOVE ONLY SLOWLY E THIS PERIOD AS ASSOCIATED NRN PLAINS UPR LOW REMAINS QSTNRY AND ATTENDANT SHORTWAVE TROUGH NOW ENTERING CHIHUAHUA SHEARS ENE ACROSS W TX...OK...AND...BY SUN MORNING...KS/MO. MID/UPR LVL SPEED MAX WITH THE CHIHUAHUA SYSTEM WILL REDEVELOP NE INTO N TX/OK BY THIS EVE...AND FURTHER EXPAND NE ACROSS MID MS VLY/UPR GRT LKS EARLY SUN. AT THE SFC...MAIN FRONTAL ZONE WILL REMAIN NEARLY STNRY FROM LWR MI TO E TX TODAY...WITH COMPOSITE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY LEFT BY OVERNIGHT STORMS LIKELY TO LIFT SLOWLY N ACROSS AR AND THE LWR TN VLY. A WAVE SHOULD FORM OVER NE TX OR THE ARKLATEX LATER TODAY...NEAR INTERSECTION OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WITH FRONT. THE WAVE SHOULD TRACK NNE INTO THE LWR OH VLY TONIGHT/EARLY SUN.

sections.title: E TX/LWR MS VLY INTO THE LWR TN/LWR OH VLYS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: WSW-ENE ORIENTED QLCS OVER THE LWR MS AND TN VLYS MAY FURTHER WEAKEN LATER THIS MORNING AS WEAK HEIGHT RISES OVERSPREAD REGION AND SFC TEMPERATURES REACH DIURNAL MINIMUMS. SFC HEATING AND CONTINUED INFLOW OF VERY MOIST AIR SHOULD...HOWEVER...SUPPORT REDEVELOPMENT OF SOME STORMS IN WHAT IS LEFT OF THE MCS BY EARLY AFTN...WITH ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE TO ITS S OVER SRN/CNTRL AR AND NRN MS. OTHER STORMS MAY FORM LATER THIS MORNING AND THIS AFTN OVER NE TX AND SE OK...AS ISENTROPIC ASCENT DOWNSTREAM FROM CHIHUAHUA UPR IMPULSE INCREASES ATOP SHALLOW FRONT. COMBINATION OF DAYTIME HEATING AND RICH MOISTURE /PW 1.50-1.75 INCHES WITH SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S/ SHOULD ALLOW FOR SUBSTANTIAL LOW LVL DESTABILIZATION ALONG AND S OF MCS OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND E OF FRONT...WITH SBCAPE EXPECTED TO BE AOA 2000 J/KG WITH MINIMAL CINH. COUPLED WITH STRONGLY-SHEARED LOW TO MID LVL WIND FIELD...SETUP COULD SUPPORT SCTD SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS WITH TORNADOES/SVR HAIL. AS THE CHIHUAHUA SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED MID/UPR LVL SPEED MAX /WITH 250 MB FLOW AROUND 150 KTS/ CONTINUE NEWD LATER THIS AFTN AND TONIGHT...DOWNSTREAM SLY LLJ SHOULD MARKEDLY INCREASE OVER THE LWR MS AN TN VLYS. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT ENHA

sections.title: MIDDLE/UPR OH VLY
sections.text: ERN END OF AFOREMENTIONED QLCS SHOULD CONTINUE E ACROSS ERN KY AND CNTRL/ERN OH THROUGH LATER THIS MORNING. DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION AND MODEST LOW LVL MOISTURE INFLOW MAY SUPPORT A MODEST SVR THREAT /DMGG WINDS OR AN ISOLD TORNADO/ THROUGH EARLY EVE. ADDITIONAL STRONG TO SVR ACTIVITY MAY AFFECT THE REGION LATE IN THE PERIOD /AFTER 06Z SUN/ AS SFC WAVE MOVES NE TOWARD THE LWR OH VLY AND ASSOCIATED LLJ STRENGTHENS OVER ERN KY/OH. ..CORFIDI/GARNER.. 05/01/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BROAD HIGH AMPLITUDE TROUGH EXTENDING FROM THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST INTO THE CENTRAL STATES WILL MOVE ONLY SLOWLY EWD THROUGH THIS PERIOD. WITHIN THIS LARGE TROUGH...A STRONG UPPER IMPULSE...WILL EJECT RAPIDLY NEWD FROM SWRN TX INTO SERN KS/SWRN MO...ALONG WITH AN ACCOMPANYING 90-100 KT MID LEVEL JET. THIS FEATURE IS EXPECTED TO BE A MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR TO AN ENHANCED SEVERE WEATHER THREAT LATER TODAY AND TONIGHT. AT THE SURFACE...MAIN FRONTAL BOUNDARY WILL REMAIN QUASI-STATIONARY FROM LOWER MI SWWD INTO ERN TX. A WEAK SURFACE LOW WILL TRACK NEWD ALONG THE FRONT...FROM NERN TX INTO AR THIS EVENING...AND INTO MO/IL OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: ERN TX...LOWER MS VALLEY...LWR TN AND OH VALLEYS
sections.text: AT MID MORNING...AN AREA OF THUNDERSTORMS EXTENDED FROM TN WWD INTO PORTIONS OF NRN MS/SERN AR...AND VERY MOIST SLY FLOW MAY MAINTAIN THIS QUASI-STATIONARY MCS THE AFTERNOON HOURS. THERE WILL BE A POTENTIAL FOR A TORNADO OR TWO...ESPECIALLY WITH THE STORMS ON THE SOUTH END OF THE COMPLEX...THOUGH TRAINING STORMS SUGGEST HEAVY RAINS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY THREAT INTO THE AFTERNOON HOURS. OTHER STORMS WILL ALSO BE DEVELOPING SOUTH OF THESE BAND OF STORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF ERN LA...MS AND NWRN AL...WITH ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS FAVORABLE FOR TORNADOES. HOWEVER...AS UPPER WAVE APPROACHES FROM THE WEST...STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO REDEVELOP NEAR THE FRONT/SURFACE LOW IN THE ARKLATEX REGION BY EARLY/MID AFTERNOON. THESE STORMS SHOULD THEN DEVELOP/SPREAD NEWD AHEAD OF THE NEWD MOVING SURFACE LOW. THESE STORMS WILL DEVELOP IN A VOLATILE ENVIRONMENT WITH VERY STRONG INSTABILITY...MLCAPES NEAR 3000 J/KG AND 60-70 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR. THESE ENVIRONMENT WILL BE SUPPORTIVE FOR INTENSE SUPERCELLS. THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY...EXTREME LOW/DEEP LAYER SHEAR FAVORS LONG LIVED AND VERY DAMAGING TORNADOES WITH THESE STORMS. THE GREATEST THREAT FOR THE VERY DAMAGING TORNADOES WILL BE IN THE ARKLATEX BY M

sections.title: MID-SOUTH TO THE MIDWEST
sections.text: SVR EVENT HAS UNFOLDED THIS EVE AS SUPERCELLS HAVE RAPIDLY FORMED OVER CNTRL/SRN AR WITHIN MLCAPES OF 3000 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR 70+ KTS. SUNSET LLVL SHEAR PARAMETERS HAVE BEEN COMPARATIVELY WEAKER THAN LAST NIGHT...BUT 0-1KM SRH WILL INCREASE AS THE LLVL FLOW ACCELERATES IN RESPONSE TO THE EJECTING TX IMPULSE. AS A RESULT...DISCRETE SUPERCELLS WILL HAVE STRONG POTENTIAL FOR PRODUCING TORNADOES...A FEW STRONG AND LONG-LIVED...PARTICULARLY ACROSS CNTRL/ERN AR ENE INTO EXTREME NWRN MS...WRN TN AND SERN MO THROUGH THE NIGHT. FARTHER N...AIR MASS WILL GRADUALLY RECOVER AS TROPICAL BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE SURGES NW TO THE PRIMARY SFC FRONT RESIDING JUST NW OF THE LWR OH RVR VLY. EXPECT THE MID-SOUTH ACTIVITY WILL DEVELOP/TRANSLATE ENE TOWARD IND/WRN OH AND AS FAR E AS CNTRL KY AND MIDDLE TN. HIGHEST TORNADO POTENTIAL WILL EXIST ACROSS THE MDT RISK AREA ALONG/E OF THE TRACK OF A SFC LOW AND AMIDST NEAR 70 DEG SFC DEW POINTS. OTHERWISE...DMGG WIND GUSTS/HAIL WILL ACCOMPANY ANY DVLPG QLCS AS FAR N AS IND/WRN OH BY 12Z.

sections.title: LWR MS VLY/TN VLY/DEEP S
sections.text: PERSISTENT H925-H85 CONFLUENCE ZONE HAS BEEN A FAVORED ZONE FOR TSTM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL MS NEWD TOWARD MIDDLE TN. THERE WILL BE SOME THREAT FOR ISOLD TORNADOES/DMGG WIND GUSTS ASSOCD WITH SUPERCELLS ACROSS THIS REGION GIVEN 50-60 KTS OF HIGH LEVEL FLOW AND 300-400 M2/S2 0-1KM SRH. ..RACY.. 05/02/2010
